meta_herb: Radix bupleuri for uncomplicated acute respiratory tract infections: a systematic review

Acute respiratory tract infections are a major cause of global morbidity and mortality, with an estimation of 2.65 million deaths worldwide. Standard treatments for uncomplicated ARTIs are mainly symptomatic, including analgesics, antipyretics, mucolytics, expectorants, decongestants, and educational interventions. Despite research has suggested uncomplicated ARTIs are predominantly viral infections, antibiotics showed little benefit in symptom improvement for ARTIs such as colds, or acute laryngitis, antibiotics are frequently prescribed in primary care settings. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an evolving major global threat to public health. The marginal benefit of antibiotics for ARTIs are outweighed by increasing AMR and common adverse reactions leading to unnecessary increases in healthcare costs. Research is warranted to explore other alternatives that may offered symptomatic relief and reduce unnecessary antibiotic prescribing.

Bupleurum chinense herbal formula for the antituberculosis drug-induced hepatotoxicity : A systematic review and meta-analysis

Tuberculosis (TB), as a global concern, seriously affects people's health. The WHO global tuberculosis report 2020 estimates that in 2019 10.0 million people fell ill with TB.  Most of the first-line drugs used in the treatment of TB have potentially hepatotoxic effects. The standard short-course chemotherapy is an effective way to control TB, which includes a combination treatment of isoniazid , rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol. Anti-TB chemotherapy often has a long course of treatment, and the combined use of multiple anti-TB medications has a heavier burden on the liver, which easily leads to patients being forced to stop treatment.  Antituberculosis drug hepatotoxicity (ATDH), which makes it difficult for patients to adhere to the entire course of chemotherapy, is the most serious adverse effect of anti-tuberculosis therapy.  As an ancient therapeutic method, Bupleurum chinense (BC, Radix Bupleuri) herbal formula has been used for thousands of years in China. Since the 1990s, there have been many clinical reports of BC formula for ATDH, and the curative effect is remarkable. However, There is a lack of systematic review on the BC formula for ATDH.

Effectiveness of the treatment on migraine in clinical controlled trials with Bupleurum analogous prescription from traditional Chinese medicine:a meta-analysis

Migraine is a common chronic neurovascular disease in clinic, which is characterized by paroxysmal, repeated attacks and difficult recovery.At present, the pathogenesis of migraine has not been fully explained, among which the vascular origin theory, trigeminal neurovascular theory, neurogenic theory and cortical diffusion inhibition theory are all recognized pathogenesis in recent years [10]. Drugs for migraine, such as triptans, ergotamines, calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor antagonists [2, 11], etc., will produce certain toxic side effects and drug resistance after long-term use of these drugs, thus affecting the curative effect and laying a hidden danger for recurrence. As the dominant disease in TCM treatment[12], this disease is indispensable in improving the overall diagnosis and treatment level of this disease. Among them, the author, combining with a large number of literature conclusions, found that the reports of treating migraine with Bupleurum prescription and shaoyang method can prove the curative effect. Therefore, this study takes the literature of Bupleurum analogous prescription for treating migraine as the research report object, and conducts meta-analysis to further clarify the clinical efficacy of treating migraine with this method as the therapeutic principle, so as to provide more reference for clinical treatment and application in the future.

"Acute respiratory tract infections are a major cause of global morbidity and mortality, with an estimation of 2.65 million deaths worldwide. Standard treatments for uncomplicated ARTIs are mainly symptomatic, including analgesics, antipyretics, mucolytics, expectorants, decongestants, and educational interventions. Despite research has suggested uncomplicated ARTIs are predominantly viral infections, antibiotics showed little benefit in symptom improvement for ARTIs such as colds, or acute laryngitis, antibiotics are frequently prescribed in primary care settings. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an evolving major global threat to public health. The marginal benefit of antibiotics for ARTIs are outweighed by increasing AMR and common adverse reactions leading to unnecessary increases in healthcare costs. The standard short-course chemotherapy is an effective way to control TB, which includes a combination treatment of isoniazid , rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol. Anti-TB chemotherapy often has a long course of treatment, and the combined use of multiple anti-TB medications has a heavier burden on the liver, which easily leads to patients being forced to stop treatment.  Antituberculosis drug hepatotoxicity (ATDH), which makes it difficult for patients to adhere to the entire course of chemotherapy, is the most serious adverse effect of anti-tuberculosis therapy.  As an ancient therapeutic method, Bupleurum chinense (BC, Radix Bupleuri) herbal formula has been used for thousands of years in China.
